correctness.rationale: The exact 1-dimensional counterexample takes H=C, one analysis map Λ=2I and Γ=0. Then A=B=4, synthesis TΛ=2I has unique right inverse TΛ†=(1/2)I, and A||TΛ†||^{-2}/(2B)=2. The source inequality is an equality at λ=1<2, although Γ is the zero family and cannot be a g-frame. For every Hilbert g-frame, the relative assumption ||(UΛ+UΓ)f||≤sqrt(λ)||UΛ f|| yields by the reverse and direct triangle inequalities the exact bounds A(1-sqrt(λ))² and B(1+sqrt(λ))² whenever 0≤λ<1. At λ≥1, Γ=0 supplies the sharp obstruction for every nonzero Hilbert space. Invertibility avoids any choice-of-pseudoinverse ambiguity. Scaling Λ by c changes the printed threshold by |c|² while the relative inequality remains invariant.
